title: Two-phase mission completes and explains
scenario: DBOS mission: check the disk, then research solar with slides (fake agents); temp SQLite store.
expected: Status 'completed'; explain starts '2 of 2 steps', contains the research findings and the deck file; the PC lock is released.

title: Failed check triggers a re-plan
scenario: open_app 'word' comes back unconfirmed (no window); the re-plan uses wordpad and types.
expected: Status 'completed', replans == 1, the re-plan context says what failed, actions word, wordpad, type into wordpad.

title: Re-plans are bounded
scenario: Every plan opens an app that never appears.
expected: Status 'failed' after exactly MAX_REPLANS (2) re-plans and 3 steps.

title: Same step, same result: loop stopped
scenario: The plan repeats 'check the disk' 8 times with an identical result.
expected: Status 'stopped' with 'same step gave the same result' after exactly 3 steps.

title: Ping-pong between two steps stopped
scenario: The plan alternates maximize/minimize Notepad 8 times.
expected: Status 'stopped' with 'undoing each other' after exactly 4 steps.

title: Step budget across re-plans
scenario: A 30-step plan (capped to 20) whose 20th step fails; the re-plan adds 10 more.
expected: Status 'stopped' with 'step budget'; exactly 20 steps recorded and 20 agent actions.

title: Time budget stops the mission
scenario: Budget 0.5 s; four checks of 0.3 s each.
expected: Status 'stopped' with 'time budget' and fewer than 4 steps run.

title: Cancel at the step boundary
scenario: missions.cancel() 0.3 s into the first of four 0.6 s steps; also cancel of an unknown id.
expected: Status 'cancelled' with 1 step; on_cancel (stop the running PC job) called once; unknown id returns False; lock released.

title: Waiting for permission stops and says how
scenario: Step 2 (typing) needs the owner's approval (id ap-42); step 3 follows.
expected: Status 'waiting_for_permission', approval_id ap-42 kept, step 3 never runs, explain names ap-42.

title: Owner denial ends the mission
scenario: Step 2 comes back state='denied'.
expected: Status 'denied', no re-plan, step 3 never runs, explain says denied.

title: Explanation carries uncertainty and the reason
scenario: A play step passes but Windows did not confirm the title; the research step fails and the re-plan has nothing.
expected: Status 'failed'; explain starts '1 of', includes 'media session did not confirm', 'Not finished', and no invented 'Findings'.

title: Side-effect journal: done, repeated, failed
scenario: missions._act types 'hello' twice with the same occurrence, once as occurrence 1; a 'flaky' typing fails then succeeds.
expected: Agent calls exactly hello, hello, flaky, flaky; the second identical call is replayed; a failed effect may run again.

title: Interrupted typing is not repeated
scenario: A full mission run finds its type_text step journaled 'started' but never finished (the process died in it).
expected: Status 'needs_owner', error says 'not repeated', the typing agent is never called, the next step does not run.

title: Interrupted open is repeated
scenario: The same, but the interrupted step is open_app (harmless to repeat).
expected: Status 'completed'; open_app runs once more, then the next step.

title: Interrupted browser click is not repeated
scenario: The interrupted step is a browser 'click' on 'Send' (it may already have sent).
expected: Status 'needs_owner'; the click is not run again.

title: Interrupted account check is repeated
scenario: The interrupted step is a browser 'whoami' (read-only).
expected: Status 'completed'; whoami runs again, then the next step.

title: Killed mid safe step: resume without repeating typing
scenario: A real process types 'once', then is SIGKILLed inside the 'slow' check; a new process launches DBOS and resumes.
expected: Status 'completed'; actions in order once, slow, slow, disk (the typing is not repeated, the check is).

title: Killed mid typing: resume stops for the owner
scenario: A real process is SIGKILLed while its type_text step runs; a new process resumes the mission.
expected: Status 'needs_owner'; actions disk, once only (typing never runs a second time, nothing after it runs).

title: Mission waits its turn for the PC
scenario: A single PC task holds the PC lock when a mission starts.
expected: Mission status 'busy' naming the task; no step runs.

title: No plan: not understood
scenario: The planner returns no steps for the goal.
expected: Status 'not_understood' with no steps.

title: Crashing agent fails the step, not the mission engine
scenario: The open_app agent raises RuntimeError every time; each re-plan picks a different app.
expected: Status 'failed' with the error class recorded in each step, and the PC lock released.

title: Executor runs independent steps in parallel
scenario: main_agent run_plan: a, b, c (0.3 s each, independent), then d needing all three; parallel=3.
expected: Done in under 0.9 s and d receives the outputs of a, b and c.

title: A failure skips only what depends on it
scenario: a fails definitely; c needs a, d needs c; b and e (needs b) are independent.
expected: a failure; c and d not_executed; b and e success.

title: Unknown result of a side effect is held
scenario: A non-idempotent 'send' step times out (0.2 s limit); 'after' depends on it; 'other' is independent; parallel=1.
expected: send unknown and held, dispatched once; after and other not_executed; run_state 'held'.

title: Read-only step retried once
scenario: A read-only step raises a transient error once, then succeeds.
expected: Outcome success after 2 attempts.

title: Definite failure of a side effect is not retried
scenario: A non-idempotent 'write' step raises StepFailed('the disk is full'); 'other' is independent.
expected: write failure after 1 attempt, not held; other succeeds.

title: Overall time limit
scenario: Four chained 0.3 s steps under a 0.5 s total limit.
expected: a succeeds; b is cut by the limit (outcome unknown, not retried); c and d not_executed; all within 1.0 s.

title: Waiting for the owner is not working time
scenario: A step polls 0.6 s for an approval and credits it with add_waiting; step limit 0.3 s, total 0.5 s. Control: the same 0.6 s without credit.
expected: The waiting step succeeds with waited >= 0.6 s; the control times out as unknown and held.

title: Cancel stops before the next step
scenario: The cancel event is set while step a runs; b needs a, c needs b.
expected: a success, b not_executed with 'cancelled', run_state 'cancelled'.

title: Resume keeps finished steps
scenario: run_plan with prior = {a: success 'saved-a'} (a has side effects); b needs a.
expected: Only b is dispatched; a keeps its saved text.

title: Resume with a held step runs nothing new
scenario: run_plan with prior = {send: unknown, held}; 'after' needs send; 'other' is independent.
expected: Nothing is dispatched; after and other not_executed.

title: Final answer is honest about each step
scenario: final_text for: send unknown+held, a success, b failure.
expected: Contains a's text, 'Needs your attention', 'did not retry', 'b (failure: model refused)'; run_state 'held'.

title: Provider error text is not passed on
scenario: A step raises ValueError whose text has a URL with a synthetic key.
expected: Outcome failure with error exactly 'ValueError'.

title: Killed run: checkpoints recovered, side effect held
scenario: A real process runs read -> send (side effect) -> after with RunStore checkpoints and is SIGKILLed during send; then recover() and resume.
expected: recover() returns r1 once; read success kept; send unknown+held; resuming dispatches nothing; run_state 'held'.

title: Corrupt and half-written checkpoints
scenario: Run folder with a corrupt JSON, a half-written .tmp, a finished run and a running run.
expected: Only the running run is recovered (its read-only step unknown, not held); corrupt/half files and '../' ids are ignored.

title: Automation does not fire twice after a restart
scenario: Kernel automation (cron 08:00 UTC) fires; the kernel database is closed and reopened at the same instant and ticked twice; the node finishes the job; then the next day.
expected: 1 run and 1 job before and after the restart; the next day's slot fires once (2 jobs).

title: Missed windows coalesce to one run
scenario: Interval 600 s, catchup 'one'; the server was off for 5 slots.
expected: Exactly 1 fired run plus a 'skipped_missed' record; 1 job.

title: Missed windows beyond grace are skipped
scenario: Interval 600 s, catchup 'skip', grace 60 s; the latest slot is 300 s old.
expected: No run fires, one 'skipped_missed' record, no job.

title: Disabled automation never fires
scenario: Created disabled; 3 slots pass; then enabled.
expected: Nothing while disabled; enabling replays nothing; the next slot fires once.

title: Claimed run whose process died is not re-run
scenario: A run is claimed, then the kernel stops before firing it; after restart the scheduler ticks within and after the 15 min grace.
expected: The crashed run stays 'claimed', then becomes 'unknown'; it never creates a job.

title: One-time automation across a restart
scenario: A 'once' automation fires, the kernel restarts, ticks again then a day later.
expected: 1 run, state 'completed', 1 job.

title: Repeated failures pause the automation
scenario: pause_after_failures=2; two runs' jobs fail.
expected: Automation disabled and 'paused' with '2 failed runs'; nothing fires afterwards.

title: Live research-deck mission on the laptop
scenario: On the laptop with the local models: 'research solar panels, make slides, open them and explain' as a mission.
expected: Completed: a deck that passed QA, a window showing it, and an explanation whose findings come from the cited sources.

title: Diamond dependencies run in order, siblings in parallel
scenario: Real executor, fake dispatcher: a -> (b, c) -> d with parallel=3; each step records when it starts and ends.
expected: b and c start only after a ended and start together; d starts only after both ended and receives exactly b's and c's outputs.
regression: Catches a scheduler that starts a step before its dependencies finished, or serialises independent siblings.

title: A failure deep in a chain stops every step after it, not the other branch
scenario: a->b->c->d->e and an independent x->y; c raises StepFailed('the page would not load') (fake dispatcher).
expected: a, b, x, y succeed; c failure; d and e not_executed and never dispatched; run_state 'partial'; the final answer carries y's output and names c, d and e with their reasons.
regression: Guards transitive skip propagation and the honest 'Not everything worked' report.

title: A send that may have happened holds everything after it
scenario: A non-idempotent 'send' raises StepUnknown('the server closed the connection after the request was sent'); 'after' needs it; 'other' is independent; parallel=1 (fake dispatcher).
expected: send dispatched once, unknown and held, not retried; after and other not_executed; run_state 'held'; the final answer says 'Needs your attention' and quotes the reason.
regression: Explicit StepUnknown path (D-024 covers only the timeout path): no duplicate send, honest hand-back.

title: Retry limit is exact and the last error is reported
scenario: A read-only step that always fails with StepFailed('upstream 503'), run with retries=2 and with retries=0 (fake dispatcher).
expected: retries=2: exactly 3 dispatches, outcome failure, attempts 3, error 'upstream 503'; retries=0: exactly 1 dispatch.
regression: Catches an off-by-one or unbounded retry loop and a lost error message.

title: No retry when the overall time limit is too close
scenario: A read-only step fails at once (fake dispatcher); total limit 1.5 s (under the 2 s retry margin) and, as control, 10 s.
expected: 1.5 s: 1 dispatch, attempts 1; 10 s: 2 dispatches (one retry).
regression: A retry must never start when it cannot finish inside the run's time budget.

title: Cancel stops retries of a failing step
scenario: The owner's cancel is set while step a raises a transient error; retries=3; b needs a; c independent; parallel=1.
expected: a dispatched exactly once (no retry after cancel); b and c not_executed, c with 'cancelled'; run_state 'cancelled'.
regression: Cancellation must win over the retry loop.

title: An unexpected error: read-only fails, side effect is held
scenario: The same RuntimeError (with detail text) from a read-only step and from a non-idempotent step (fake dispatcher).
expected: read-only: failure after 2 attempts, not held; side effect: unknown, held, 1 attempt; errors are the class name only.
regression: Guards the outcome rules for generic exceptions and that provider text never leaks.

title: Parallel limit is respected
scenario: 6 independent 0.1 s steps with parallel=2 (fake dispatcher counts concurrent calls).
expected: Peak concurrency exactly 2; all succeed; takes at least 3 rounds (>= 0.28 s).
regression: Catches an executor that ignores the semaphore and floods tools or providers.

title: A hanging read is timed out, retried once, and its dependents skipped
scenario: Read-only step sleeps 1 s with a 0.2 s step limit; b needs it (fake dispatcher).
expected: Dispatched exactly twice; outcome unknown, not held; b not_executed ('did not finish'); whole run under 1.5 s.
regression: Bounded per-step time and bounded retry for hung reads.

title: Cancelled before start: nothing runs
scenario: The cancel event is already set when run_plan starts (a, b needs a, c; fake dispatcher).
expected: Nothing dispatched; every step not_executed with a cancel/skip reason; run_state 'cancelled'.
regression: A stop pressed before work begins must start nothing.

title: The overall limit stops the running child
scenario: A 5 s fake dispatcher under a 0.4 s overall limit; the dispatcher records whether it finished or was cancelled.
expected: The child coroutine is cancelled (not left running), outcome unknown after 1 attempt, run returns in under 1.5 s.
regression: Timed-out work must actually be stopped, not orphaned.

title: A crashing progress callback never stops the work
scenario: on_start and on_progress both raise RuntimeError (the UI went away); a -> b (fake dispatcher).
expected: Both steps succeed.
regression: Reporting failures (UI, persistence hooks) must not abort a long task.

title: When nothing worked the answer says so
scenario: Both steps of a plan raise StepFailed (fake dispatcher); final_text of the real run.
expected: Answer starts 'I could not finish this:' and names both failures; run_state 'failed'; no 'Not everything worked' (which implies partial success).
regression: Never a success-sounding summary for a run with no result.

title: A lost step result is never reported as done
scenario: run_state for a 3-step plan with only 2 (successful) results, and with all 3.
expected: 2 of 3 -> 'partial'; 3 of 3 -> 'done'.
regression: Catches 'done' computed from the results present instead of the plan.

title: Resume keeps a definite failure and runs only independent work
scenario: run_plan with prior {a: failure 'the disk is full'} (a has side effects); b needs a; c independent (fake dispatcher).
expected: Only c is dispatched; a keeps its failure text; b not_executed; run_state 'partial'.
regression: A resumed run must not silently redo or forget a failed side effect.

title: Checkpoints restore every step result exactly
scenario: Plan a -> b checkpointed to a real RunStore after each step (a needs 2 attempts, b reports waiting time); another RunStore instance loads it as prior for a -> b -> c (fake dispatcher).
expected: Restored results equal the originals (outcome, text, attempts 2, waited); only c is dispatched on resume.
regression: Guards the checkpoint format: attempts and waiting time must survive a restart.

title: Killed during a read: resume repeats the read, never the send
scenario: A real process runs send (side effect) -> fetch (read) -> report with checkpoints and is SIGKILLed during fetch; recover(); resume with the plugin's rule (read-only unknowns run again).
expected: send success kept; fetch unknown but not held; resume dispatches fetch and report only; 'send' happened exactly once in total; run_state 'done'.
regression: Complements D-034 (killed during the send): a harmless step is redone, a side effect is not.

title: Recovery is idempotent and keeps finished steps
scenario: A checkpoint lists a and b as running although a already has a success (crash between the two writes); recover() twice.
expected: First restart: a stays success, b unknown (not held), state 'interrupted'; second restart recovers nothing and changes nothing.
regression: Repeated restarts must not degrade finished steps or re-mark results.

title: A crash while writing a checkpoint keeps the previous one
scenario: RunStore saves step 1, then the save of step 2 dies after writing the temp file (fake: os.replace raises OSError).
expected: The save raises; load() returns the whole step-1 checkpoint; the half-written temp file is never listed as a run.
regression: Guards atomic replace: a power cut never leaves an unreadable or half run.

title: Cancel during planning: no step runs
scenario: DBOS mission whose planner takes 0.6 s; missions.cancel() at 0.2 s (fake agents).
expected: Status 'cancelled', no steps, the agent is never called, explain says 'Not finished', PC lock released.
regression: A stop that arrives before the first step must still stop the mission.

title: Effect done before the crash is replayed, not repeated
scenario: The journal already has type_text 'done' (ok) for this mission (the process died after typing, before DBOS recorded the step); the mission is resumed (fake agents).
expected: Status 'completed'; the typing agent is never called; step 1 is marked replayed; step 2 runs.
regression: The other half of D-013: a finished effect is reported from the journal, never typed twice.

title: The same step planned twice runs twice
scenario: Plan: type '-----', check disk, type '-----' again (fake agents).
expected: Status 'completed'; agent calls exactly '-----', disk, '-----' (each occurrence is its own effect).
regression: Guards against over-eager de-duplication that would silently drop intended work.

title: A planner crash ends the mission honestly
scenario: The mission's planner raises RuntimeError (fake planner).
expected: Within 8 s the mission record has a final, non-'completed' status (not 'queued'/'running') and the PC lock is free.
regression: The owner must never see 'queued' forever for a mission that already died.

title: The retry budget survives kernel restarts
scenario: A task with max_attempts 2 on a real kernel database; the kernel is closed and reopened between attempts.
expected: After two restarts a third attempt and another repair are refused ('budget'); the task ends failed with attempts 2 and the honest result.
regression: Catches a budget kept in memory that a restart would reset.

title: An expired task says why, even after a partial result
scenario: A running task reported 'draft of page 1 of 3 written'; its deadline passes and Tasks.expire runs.
expected: State 'failed'; the result names the time budget AND keeps the partial result.
regression: Found 2026-10-17: the partial result alone read like the outcome (fixed in tasks.py).

title: A final task stays final under late reports
scenario: Tasks ended cancelled, completed and failed; a late runner then reports running, completed, failed and verifying.
expected: Every late report is refused; state and result unchanged; exactly one final audit row per task.
regression: A cancelled task must never be resurrected or relabelled by a slow worker.

title: A fresh session's checkpoint tells the truth
scenario: One task failed after 2 attempts (page 2 returns 500), one still running; Tasks.checkpoint for the agent.
expected: The failed task shows state failed, attempts 2/3, the blocker and next 'tell the owner the exact blocker'; the running one says to wait.
regression: What a compacted session reads must not hide a failure or invent progress.

title: Owner cancels while the lab works
scenario: Real kernel + runner endpoints on 127.0.0.1, fake lab runner: dispatch, attempt 1 starts, the owner cancels the task, the runner reports and finishes.
expected: Runner status 'cancelled'; its later 'verifying' report 409; finish accepted; the task stays cancelled; the lab job is failed.
regression: The owner's stop wins over the lab's progress.

title: A crashed lab run does not leave the task 'running'
scenario: Fake lab runner starts attempt 1, then crashes and only posts finish {ok: false, 'runner error: KeyError'}.
expected: The task is failed at once with that error in its result (not 'running' until its deadline).
regression: Found 2026-10-17: only final tasks are announced, so the owner heard nothing for hours (fixed in jobs.py).

title: An unclaimed lab job that expired fails its task
scenario: The lab runner is offline (fake: never polls); the queued lab job passes its TTL; the kernel's sweep runs.
expected: Sweep expires 1 job; the task is failed and its result says the job expired (not 'queued').
regression: Found 2026-10-17 (fixed in jobs.py).

title: Cancelling a queued lab job cancels its task
scenario: The owner cancels the queued lab job through the owner plane (cancel_job).
expected: Job cancelled; task 'cancelled'; the runner is then handed nothing.
regression: Found 2026-10-17: the task kept saying 'queued: the lab will start it' (fixed in jobs.py).

title: Kill switch: the lab runner gets no new work
scenario: A lab job is queued; the kill switch is on; the fake runner polls /v1/jarvis/runner/next; then the switch is lifted.
expected: While killed no job is handed out and it stays queued; after resume the runner gets it.
regression: Found 2026-10-17: the runner path handed out jobs while killed (fixed in Jobs.next_for).

title: No second lab dispatch after a kernel restart
scenario: A task is dispatched; the kernel process is replaced (new connection and handler on the same data); the agent dispatches again.
expected: The second dispatch is refused 409; exactly one lab job exists.
regression: Duplicate-dispatch protection must live in the database, not in process memory.

title: A refused lab dispatch fails the automation's task
scenario: A lab-task automation fires; the lab path (fake dispatch) answers 409 'the lab is busy'.
expected: Run 'refused' with the reason; the created task is failed with 'not dispatched: ...' (not left 'planning').
regression: Unattended work that never started must be reported as such.

title: An automation whose job the owner cancelled keeps running later
scenario: Interval automation (overlap 'skip', the default) fires; the owner cancels its queued job; the next slot comes.
expected: The next slot fires (a second job is queued); the cancelled run is settled, not left 'fired'.
regression: A cancelled job must not block every later run of its automation.

title: Kill switch stops automations; resume fires the slot once
scenario: A slot is due; the kill switch is on; run_now and tick are tried; then resume and two ticks.
expected: run_now refused 503; nothing fires or is recorded while killed; after resume exactly one run and one job.
regression: Neither lost nor doubled work across a kill/resume.

title: A command automation waits for JARVIS and fires once
scenario: JARVIS (fake agent) is busy when the slot comes; ticks while busy; then it is free and the scheduler ticks three more times.
expected: While busy the run stays 'claimed'; afterwards exactly one command row and one agent call.
regression: Retry-until-free must not fire the same run twice.

title: Waiting for a busy JARVIS is bounded
scenario: JARVIS (fake agent) stays busy past the 15 min claim grace.
expected: The run becomes 'failed' ('JARVIS stayed busy too long'), counts one failure, and never fires afterwards.
regression: Bounded retry for deferred unattended work.

title: Daily run limit bounds a catch-up burst
scenario: Interval 600 s, catchup 'all', overlap 'queue', max 3 runs per day; the server was off for 10 slots.
expected: Exactly 3 runs fire and 3 jobs are queued; the other 7 slots are recorded 'skipped_limit'.
regression: A long outage must not unleash a flood of side effects.

title: Deadline during a lab run stops the runner honestly
scenario: Fake lab runner is in attempt 1 when the task's deadline passes; it reports, checks status and finishes.
expected: The report is refused 409; status says 'failed'; the task is failed with 'time budget used up'; finish accepted.
regression: Long tasks end at their budget even while a worker is busy.
